events.title: Mount Vesuvius Buries Pompeii and Herculaneum
events.description: According to the traditional date, Vesuvius erupted violently and buried the Roman towns of Pompeii and Herculaneum under ash and volcanic debris. Thousands of people died, and the cities lay hidden for centuries.
events.significance: The buried cities were preserved in remarkable detail. Their excavation gave us an unmatched view of everyday life in the Roman world.

events.title: St. Bartholomew's Day Massacre Begins
events.description: In Paris, Catholic mobs and royal forces began killing Huguenot (French Protestant) leaders and followers. The violence spread to other French cities over the following weeks.
events.significance: It was one of the deadliest episodes of the French Wars of Religion. It deepened the divide between Catholics and Protestants in France for a generation.

events.title: British Forces Burn Washington
events.description: During the War of 1812, British troops captured Washington, D.C., and set fire to public buildings, including the Capitol and the White House.
events.significance: It was the only time a foreign power has captured and occupied the U.S. capital. The attack became a lasting symbol of the war's low point for the young republic.

events.title: Pluto Is Reclassified as a Dwarf Planet
events.description: The International Astronomical Union voted to adopt a formal definition of "planet". Under it, Pluto no longer qualified and was designated a dwarf planet.
events.significance: The decision reshaped how we classify the solar system. It also sparked a public debate that continues today.
